The testRemoveChildren test omits a getChildCount call before remove.

The stale cache bug only surfaces when getChildCount is called while children exist, filling the cache with a stale count. If setFirstChild clears the cache first, removeChildren leaves childCount at MIN_VALUE, and getChildCount simply recounts zero.

This uncovered bug is real and untested. It leaves the API inconsistent: hasChildren() returns false while getChildCount still reports the old count. I will check whether removeChildren is used in production code.

I will search the checkstyle package for removeChildren callers. I am weighing a limited directory walk against a safer file scan.

I will run a Python scan for removeChildren calls in src/main/java to gauge production impact. If only tests invoke it, the severity is low. If production grammar code calls it after getChildCount, the bug is more serious. I also verified that childCount defaults to 0 and is lazily initialized, so fresh nodes report the correct count unless firstChild is set outside the API.

A second stale-cache bug exists in removeChildren. It does not clear branchTokenTypes. After removing children, branchContains may still return true because the cached bitset still includes the old child token types. This mirrors the childCount invalidation issue.
